questions.question: Which three systems were tested together for the first time on Artemis I?
answers: Orion, a lunar rover, and a crewed lander
SLS, a space station, and a lunar rover
Orion, a lunar lander, and a docking station
SLS, Orion, and supporting ground systems
questions.explanation: Artemis I was the first integrated flight test of SLS, Orion, and the ground systems.

questions.question: Who was aboard Orion during Artemis I?
answers: A crew practicing commercial-lander docking
Two astronauts preparing a lunar landing
Four astronauts conducting life-support tests
Instrumented test payloads, with no astronaut crew
questions.explanation: Artemis I was uncrewed; instrumented payloads collected information before astronauts flew.

questions.question: What does the abbreviation SLS mean?
answers: Space Landing System
Space Launch System
Surface Launch Spacecraft
Space Life-Support
questions.explanation: SLS stands for Space Launch System, the rocket used to launch Artemis I.

questions.question: What was Orion's role on Artemis I?
answers: The ground equipment that fueled the rocket
The deep-space spacecraft being flight-tested
The small satellite released to explore the Moon
The rocket that lifted the mission from Earth
questions.explanation: Orion is the spacecraft; SLS is its launch rocket.

questions.question: What did the Exploration Ground Systems support on Artemis I?
answers: Preparing, launching, and recovering the spacecraft
Generating electricity throughout Orion's lunar orbit
Steering Orion using onboard rocket engines
Protecting Orion during atmospheric reentry
questions.explanation: Ground systems supported mission preparation, launch, and recovery rather than flying as part of Orion.

questions.question: On which date did Artemis I launch?
answers: November 16, 2022
December 11, 2023
November 16, 2023
December 11, 2022
questions.explanation: Artemis I launched on November 16, 2022.

questions.question: Where did Artemis I lift off?
answers: Johnson Space Center in Texas
Stennis Space Center in Mississippi
Marshall Space Flight Center in Alabama
Kennedy Space Center in Florida
questions.explanation: SLS and Orion launched from Pad 39B at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida.

questions.question: When did Orion return to Earth at the end of Artemis I?
answers: November 26, 2022
December 11, 2022
November 16, 2022
December 11, 2023
questions.explanation: Orion splashed down on December 11, 2022, completing the Artemis I flight.

questions.question: Where did the Artemis I Orion capsule splash down?
answers: The Pacific Ocean off California
The Atlantic Ocean off Florida
The Gulf of Mexico off Texas
The Indian Ocean near Australia
questions.explanation: Orion splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.

questions.question: Approximately how long did Artemis I last?
answers: Two days
Ninety days
Twenty-five and a half days
Ten days
questions.explanation: The mission lasted 25 days, 10 hours, and 53 minutes, approximately 25.5 days.

questions.question: Which orbit was the main destination for Artemis I testing?
answers: A low lunar orbit followed by a surface landing
A distant retrograde orbit around the Moon
A low Earth orbit near a space station
A stationary orbit directly above the launch pad
questions.explanation: Artemis I used a distant retrograde orbit around the Moon to test Orion in deep space.

questions.question: Why is Artemis I's lunar orbit called retrograde?
answers: Orion moved opposite the direction the Moon travels around Earth
Orion remained directly above one place on the lunar surface
Orion moved in the same direction the Moon travels around Earth
Orion reversed direction each time it passed behind the Moon
questions.explanation: Retrograde describes the orbit's direction relative to the Moon's movement around Earth.

questions.question: Why was a distant retrograde orbit useful for the Artemis I test?
answers: Its low altitude allowed the capsule to practice surface landings
It kept Orion inside Earth's protective magnetic field throughout
It kept Orion within ordinary Earth-orbit GPS coverage
Its stability allowed extended testing with little station-keeping fuel
questions.explanation: The stable orbit let Orion spend time in deep space while using relatively little fuel to maintain its orbit.

questions.question: What did the trans-lunar injection burn do on Artemis I?
answers: Slow Orion for its final ocean splashdown
Separate the crew module before atmospheric entry
Put Orion on a course from Earth orbit toward the Moon
Insert Orion directly into its distant lunar orbit
questions.explanation: Trans-lunar injection increased Orion's speed and placed it on its journey toward the Moon.

questions.question: How did lunar flybys help shape Orion's Artemis I trajectory?
answers: The flybys replaced every planned engine burn
The flybys kept Orion in low Earth orbit
The Moon's gravity assisted changes in Orion's path
The Moon's atmosphere slowed Orion before orbit entry
questions.explanation: Lunar gravity assists worked with engine burns to guide Orion into lunar orbit and toward home.

questions.question: Which description correctly states what Artemis I did near the Moon?
answers: Landed a robotic Orion capsule on the Moon
Delivered astronauts who remained on the surface
Flew past and orbited the Moon without landing
Docked Orion to a crewed lunar lander
questions.explanation: Artemis I tested Orion around the Moon but did not land on its surface.

questions.question: Which set of functions did Orion's service module provide on Artemis I?
answers: Atmospheric braking, parachutes, and ocean flotation
Launch-pad fueling, tracking, and rocket assembly
Crew seating, pressure suits, and splashdown recovery
Electrical power, propulsion, and thermal control
questions.explanation: The service module supported Orion with electricity, propulsion, and temperature control.

questions.question: Which space agency provided Orion's European Service Module?
answers: The European Space Agency
The Indian Space Research Organisation
The Canadian Space Agency
The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency
questions.explanation: ESA, the European Space Agency, provided Orion's service module.

questions.question: How did Orion generate electrical power during the Artemis I mission?
answers: Solar arrays converted sunlight into electricity
Onboard batteries alone supplied the whole lunar journey
A fuel-cell system supplied the entire electrical output
Chemical rocket engines continuously drove an electrical generator
questions.explanation: Orion's service module used solar array wings to generate electricity from sunlight.

questions.question: Why was testing the heat shield during return from the Moon especially important?
answers: Lunar-return entry avoids the heating that occurs from Earth orbit
The heat shield was needed to slow Orion during its lunar flyby
Lunar-return entry is faster and hotter than entry from low Earth orbit
The heat shield generated the electricity needed for the return flight
questions.explanation: Returning at lunar speeds exposed Orion's heat shield to conditions more severe than a low-Earth-orbit return.

questions.question: How does Orion's ablative heat-shield material protect the capsule?
answers: It opens like a parachute to stop atmospheric heating
It wears away in a controlled way, carrying heat away
It prevents the atmosphere from slowing the capsule
It converts reentry heat into the spacecraft's electricity
questions.explanation: The heat shield's material ablates, or burns away in a controlled fashion, helping remove heat.

questions.question: What was the main purpose of Orion's parachutes during the Artemis I return?
answers: Provide the first braking while Orion was still in deep space
Keep the service module attached through atmospheric entry
Slow the capsule for its final descent and splashdown
Place Orion into its distant orbit around the Moon
questions.explanation: After atmospheric braking, parachutes slowed Orion for a controlled ocean splashdown.

questions.question: When did the crew module separate from the service module on the Artemis I return?
answers: After the recovery ship secured the capsule
Shortly before entering Earth's atmosphere
After the capsule had splashed down
Before the launch rocket left the ground
questions.explanation: The crew module separated before reentry; the service module did not return intact.

questions.question: Which main part of Orion was recovered after Artemis I?
answers: The European Service Module alone
The crew module
The complete crew-and-service-module stack
The launch abort tower
questions.explanation: The crew module was the part of Orion designed to return intact and be recovered.

questions.question: Why was recovering the Artemis I capsule important even though data had been sent to Earth during flight?
answers: The capsule had to be recovered before the heat shield was tested
Recovery was needed to begin the mission's lunar-orbit phase
Engineers could inspect flown hardware and retrieve onboard records
The spacecraft could not transmit any information until recovery
questions.explanation: Hardware inspections and onboard records gave engineers additional evidence about the spacecraft's performance.

questions.question: What did sensors in Commander Moonikin Campos's seat measure?
answers: Acceleration and vibration
The amount of water beneath the Moon's surface
The speed of ocean currents at the landing site
Only the chemical composition of lunar rocks
questions.explanation: Sensors recorded acceleration and vibration to help engineers understand conditions experienced by a future crew.

questions.question: What did the phantom torsos Helga and Zohar help investigate on Artemis I?
answers: How rocket engines ignite on the launch pad
The composition of lunar surface samples
How parachutes inflate after ocean splashdown
Radiation exposure during a lunar mission
questions.explanation: The human-like torsos carried radiation detectors to study exposure during deep-space travel.

questions.question: Why did Zohar wear a radiation-protection vest while Helga did not?
answers: To compare the fuel consumption of the two torsos
To determine which torso would control Orion's navigation
To compare radiation measurements with and without the vest
To let only one torso record spacecraft vibration
questions.explanation: Using otherwise similar torsos with different shielding helped test the vest's protective effect.

questions.question: What were the CubeSats carried as secondary payloads on Artemis I?
answers: Docking adapters for transferring astronauts between spacecraft
Small crew capsules that served as backups for Orion
Small satellites for independent science and technology investigations
Miniature rocket engines used to steer the main capsule
questions.explanation: CubeSats are small satellites that carried their own science and technology experiments.

questions.question: How many CubeSats rode on Artemis I?
answers: Ten
Four
Two
Twenty
questions.explanation: Artemis I carried ten CubeSats as secondary payloads.

questions.question: Which navigation challenge did Artemis I's deep-space route test?
answers: Guiding a lunar rover between surface landmarks
Keeping Orion directly above a fixed location on Earth
Guiding a lunar landing using a surface beacon
Navigating beyond the normal coverage of Earth-orbit GPS satellites
questions.explanation: The deep-space route required navigation beyond the normal coverage of GPS satellites orbiting Earth.

questions.question: What did NASA find about the European Service Module's power performance on Artemis I?
answers: It generated less power and consumed more than predicted
It generated more power and consumed less than predicted
Both generation and consumption were lower than predicted
Both generation and consumption exactly matched predictions
questions.explanation: NASA reported that the service module generated 20% more power and consumed about 25% less than predicted.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Orion's launch abort system?
answers: Pull the crew module away from a dangerous launch emergency
Insert Orion into its distant lunar orbit
Generate power while Orion is behind the Moon
Slow the capsule for its final ocean splashdown
questions.explanation: The launch abort system is designed to separate the capsule from a dangerous rocket during launch or ascent.

questions.question: Why were radiation measurements outside Earth's magnetic protection useful on Artemis I?
answers: They measured the heating experienced during atmospheric entry
They measured the mechanical loads experienced during launch
They measured the cabin pressure during a surface landing
They helped assess conditions future lunar crews would experience
questions.explanation: Artemis I measured deep-space radiation conditions relevant to protecting astronauts on later crewed flights.

questions.question: Approximately how far did Orion travel over the entire Artemis I mission?
answers: 14 million miles, or 23 million kilometers
1.4 million miles, or 2.3 million kilometers
14,000 miles, or 23,000 kilometers
140,000 miles, or 230,000 kilometers
questions.explanation: Orion traveled approximately 1.4 million miles, or 2.3 million kilometers, over its complete flight path.

questions.question: Some Orion test objectives were added during the Artemis I flight. What does this show?
answers: The team could evaluate only objectives written before launch
Teams could use available opportunities to collect additional test data
The added objectives replaced every original mission objective
Adding objectives meant earlier test data could no longer be used
questions.explanation: The flight team added useful tests while continuing the mission, increasing what engineers could learn.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly orders major Artemis I mission phases?
answers: Departure toward the Moon, return, launch, lunar orbit
Launch, splashdown, lunar orbit, departure toward the Moon
Lunar orbit, launch, splashdown, departure toward the Moon
Launch, departure toward the Moon, lunar orbit, return and splashdown
questions.explanation: Artemis I launched from Earth, traveled to lunar orbit, then returned for an ocean splashdown.

questions.question: Why test SLS, Orion, and ground systems together rather than rely only on separate tests?
answers: Their connections and coordinated operation also needed verification
Verifying components separately also proves every connection works in flight
Only the launch rocket requires testing under actual flight conditions
An integrated flight provides the same information as testing each part alone
questions.explanation: An integrated flight tests how systems work together as well as how individual parts perform.

questions.question: Which capability was not fully demonstrated by the uncrewed Artemis I flight?
answers: Launching Orion on the SLS rocket
Flying Orion around the Moon and returning it
Recovering Orion after an ocean splashdown
Supporting a living astronaut crew with critical life-support systems
questions.explanation: Critical crew life-support testing was part of Artemis II, which carried astronauts.

questions.question: Which statement correctly relates Orion's earlier test flight to Artemis I?
answers: Artemis I preceded Orion's 2014 test flight
Orion's 2014 test already carried astronauts around the Moon
Orion flew in 2014 before its first integrated flight with SLS on Artemis I
The earlier test was a crewed docking demonstration with commercial landers
questions.explanation: Orion first flew on Exploration Flight Test-1 in 2014; Artemis I was its first integrated flight with SLS.

questions.question: What new capability did Artemis II test after the uncrewed Artemis I flight?
answers: Operating SLS and Orion with astronauts aboard
Docking Orion with a lunar lander in Earth orbit
Landing Orion on the Moon
Launching SLS for the first time without a crew
questions.explanation: Artemis II was the first crewed flight test of SLS and Orion.

questions.question: How many astronauts flew on Artemis II?
answers: Six
Three
Four
Two
questions.explanation: Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen formed the four-person crew.

questions.question: Who commanded the Artemis II mission?
answers: Victor Glover
Jeremy Hansen
Christina Koch
Reid Wiseman
questions.explanation: NASA astronaut Reid Wiseman was the mission commander.

questions.question: Which Artemis II astronaut served as Orion's pilot?
answers: Christina Koch
Jeremy Hansen
Reid Wiseman
Victor Glover
questions.explanation: Victor Glover was the Artemis II pilot.

questions.question: Which pair served as the Artemis II mission specialists?
answers: Jeremy Hansen and Reid Wiseman
Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen
Reid Wiseman and Victor Glover
Victor Glover and Christina Koch
questions.explanation: Koch and Hansen were mission specialists; Wiseman commanded and Glover piloted.

questions.question: Which space agency did Artemis II astronaut Jeremy Hansen represent?
answers: European Space Agency
NASA
Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency
Canadian Space Agency
questions.explanation: Hansen flew as the Canadian Space Agency's member of the crew.

questions.question: Approximately how long did the Artemis II mission last?
answers: Two days
Six months
Twenty-five days
Ten days
questions.explanation: Artemis II's journey around the Moon and back lasted approximately ten days.

questions.question: Which description best matches Artemis II's lunar flight?
answers: A crewed landing followed by a surface expedition
A crewed flyby around the Moon and back to Earth
An uncrewed mission left permanently in lunar orbit
A mission remaining entirely in low Earth orbit
questions.explanation: Artemis II carried astronauts around the Moon without landing.

questions.question: On which date did Artemis II launch?
answers: April 1, 2026
November 16, 2022
April 10, 2026
December 11, 2022
questions.explanation: Artemis II launched from Kennedy Space Center on April 1, 2026.

questions.question: Which event completed Artemis II on April 10, 2026?
answers: Orion's splashdown in the Pacific Ocean
Orion's first departure from Earth orbit
The SLS rocket's liftoff from Florida
The crew's lunar flyby
questions.explanation: The crew returned to Earth with a Pacific Ocean splashdown on April 10.

questions.question: Where did Artemis II launch?
answers: Marshall Space Flight Center in Alabama
Johnson Space Center in Texas
Ames Research Center in California
Kennedy Space Center in Florida
questions.explanation: Kennedy Space Center was the mission's launch site.

questions.question: Which launch pad supported the Artemis II liftoff?
answers: Space Launch Complex 40
Launch Pad 39B
Launch Pad 39A
Space Launch Complex 41
questions.explanation: SLS launched Artemis II from Kennedy's Launch Pad 39B.

questions.question: Which rocket launched the Artemis II crew aboard Orion?
answers: Space Launch System
Delta IV Heavy
Atlas V
Falcon 9
questions.explanation: The crew launched on NASA's SLS, the Space Launch System.

questions.question: Which part of Orion provided the pressurized living and working space for Artemis II astronauts?
answers: The launch abort tower
The crew module
The unpressurized service module
The SLS core stage
questions.explanation: The crew module is Orion's pressurized capsule, where its astronauts live and work.

questions.question: What name did the crew give the Artemis II Orion spacecraft?
answers: Freedom
Resilience
Endeavour
Integrity
questions.explanation: The crew named its Orion spacecraft Integrity.

questions.question: Why did Artemis II conduct spacecraft checkouts near Earth before heading to the Moon?
answers: To perform an uncrewed flight before allowing astronauts to board
To verify critical systems while the crew was still close to home
To complete a full surface-landing rehearsal using Orion
To wait for Orion to dock with a commercial lunar lander
questions.explanation: The initial Earth-orbit phase allowed critical systems to be checked before the lunar journey.

questions.question: Which process was essential to Orion's cabin air system during Artemis II?
answers: Adding oxygen without removing the crew's exhaled carbon dioxide
Controlling temperature without managing the cabin's air chemistry
Removing carbon dioxide while maintaining breathable air
Removing oxygen while leaving carbon dioxide in the cabin
questions.explanation: Life support must supply breathable air and remove the carbon dioxide produced by the crew.

questions.question: Which pair of cabin conditions did Orion's life-support system actively manage?
answers: Rocket thrust and fuel-tank pressure
Solar-array angle and radio frequency
Carbon dioxide level and humidity
Orbital altitude and flight direction
questions.explanation: Life support managed carbon dioxide and humidity to maintain a safe cabin environment.

questions.question: What did Artemis II's manual piloting demonstration evaluate?
answers: The upper stage's ability to dock automatically with Orion
Ground controllers' ability to fly Orion without any crew input
The astronauts' ability to pilot a lunar lander during descent
The crew's ability to control Orion's motion and orientation
questions.explanation: Manual piloting tested how astronauts controlled Orion's flight path and orientation.

questions.question: What served as the target for Artemis II's early proximity-operations demonstration?
answers: The Moon's surface
A docked lunar lander
The International Space Station
The separated SLS upper stage
questions.explanation: The separated interim cryogenic propulsion stage served as a reference target for manual piloting.

questions.question: What is the safety advantage of Artemis II's free-return trajectory?
answers: Its path keeps Orion in lunar orbit until another spacecraft retrieves it
Its path avoids atmospheric entry by returning directly to a launch pad
Its path uses gravity to bring Orion back toward Earth after passing the Moon
Its path removes every need for navigation and trajectory checks
questions.explanation: A free-return path takes the spacecraft around the Moon and naturally back toward Earth.

questions.question: Which international agency provided Orion's European Service Module for Artemis II?
answers: Canadian Space Agency
European Space Agency
NASA acting without an international partner
Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency
questions.explanation: ESA provided the European Service Module as part of its cooperation with NASA.

questions.question: What kind of eclipse did the Artemis II crew observe during the lunar flyby?
answers: An annular solar eclipse
A total solar eclipse
A total lunar eclipse
A partial lunar eclipse
questions.explanation: The crew saw the Moon completely cover the Sun during a total solar eclipse lasting nearly an hour.

questions.question: Which set of supplies did the European Service Module provide to Orion's crew module?
answers: Drinking water, helium, and methane
Water, helium, and carbon dioxide
Water, oxygen, and nitrogen
Liquid hydrogen, methane, and nitrogen
questions.explanation: The service module supplied drinking water and the oxygen and nitrogen needed by the crew.

questions.question: Which service-module function helped maintain suitable spacecraft temperatures on Artemis II?
answers: Parachute deployment
Thermal control
Guidance and navigation
Communications and tracking
questions.explanation: Thermal control was one of the service module's key functions, alongside propulsion and power.

questions.question: What happened to Orion's service module before the crew returned through Earth's atmosphere?
answers: It docked again with the SLS upper stage
It separated only after ocean recovery
It separated from the crew module
It remained attached throughout atmospheric entry
questions.explanation: The service module detached before atmospheric entry, exposing the crew module's heat shield.

questions.question: What was the main job of Orion's heat shield during Artemis II's return?
answers: Supply propulsion for the return trajectory correction
Protect the capsule and crew from the heat of atmospheric entry
Keep the capsule upright after splashdown
Slow the capsule during the final parachute descent
questions.explanation: The heat shield protected Orion and its astronauts during the hot return through Earth's atmosphere.

questions.question: What role did Orion's parachutes play near the end of Artemis II?
answers: Slow and stabilize the capsule before splashdown
Provide the heat protection needed during atmospheric entry
Perform the final return trajectory correction burn
Keep the capsule upright after it reached the ocean
questions.explanation: Parachutes slowed and stabilized Orion after atmospheric entry and before ocean landing.

questions.question: In which ocean did the Artemis II crew return to Earth?
answers: The Indian Ocean
The Arctic Ocean
The Pacific Ocean
The Atlantic Ocean
questions.explanation: Orion splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the California coast.

questions.question: Who helped recover the Artemis II astronauts after splashdown?
answers: A combined NASA and U.S. military recovery team
An ESA and European naval recovery team
A commercial lunar-lander operations team
A NASA and Canadian military recovery team
questions.explanation: NASA and U.S. military personnel assisted the astronauts in the Pacific recovery operation.

questions.question: Which ship received the Artemis II crew after their ocean recovery?
answers: USS John P. Murtha
USS Hornet
USS Intrepid
USS Midway
questions.explanation: Helicopters transported the recovered astronauts to USS John P. Murtha.

questions.question: Why did Artemis II test Deep Space Network communications before leaving the vicinity of Earth?
answers: To confirm communication and navigation support beyond near-Earth satellite coverage
To rely only on GPS signals throughout the lunar flyby
To keep the mission inside near-Earth satellite coverage
To replace all onboard navigation with ground photography
questions.explanation: The mission checked deep-space communication and navigation capabilities while still near Earth.

questions.question: Why were Artemis II astronauts trained to describe lunar color, brightness, and texture?
answers: They measure radiation levels inside the crew cabin
They help researchers evaluate astronaut sleep patterns
They provide the main measurements of propulsion fuel consumption
These observations provide clues to the surface's composition and geologic history
questions.explanation: Detailed observations help scientists interpret the Moon's materials and the processes that shaped them.

questions.question: What did wrist monitors in Artemis II's human-research program help researchers study?
answers: Astronaut movement and sleep
Changes in the Moon's surface temperature
Cabin oxygen and carbon dioxide levels
Radiation outside the spacecraft
questions.explanation: The research program used wrist monitors to collect information about activity and sleep in deep space.

questions.question: Why was radiation-shelter practice included in Artemis II's mission plan?
answers: To reduce the acceleration felt during atmospheric entry
To replace the capsule's thermal protection during reentry
To test how crew and supplies could be arranged for protection during high-radiation events
To provide extra breathable air during the rocket launch
questions.explanation: The mission plan included rehearsing radiation protection using Orion's existing supplies and equipment.

questions.question: Why did Artemis II include a compact flywheel exercise device?
answers: To remove carbon dioxide and humidity from cabin air
To regulate cabin pressure during the lunar flyby
To shield astronauts from solar radiation
To help astronauts maintain physical conditioning during microgravity flight
questions.explanation: Exercise helps counter the effects of microgravity on muscles, bones, and physical fitness.

questions.question: Why could Artemis II meet its main flight objectives without a lunar landing?
answers: It was an uncrewed test of lunar surface equipment
It focused on crewed spacecraft tests and a lunar flyby rather than surface operations
Its main objective was docking with a commercial lander in Earth orbit
It was designed only to test launch-pad systems
questions.explanation: Artemis II was a crewed test flight around the Moon, so its objectives did not require landing.

questions.question: During the lunar flyby, why could Artemis II astronauts sometimes lose direct radio contact with Earth?
answers: Orion depended on near-Earth satellites for every radio connection
The crew had to switch off communications for the entire lunar journey
The Moon could block the radio path between Orion and Earth
The Moon's far-side atmosphere absorbed the radio signals
questions.explanation: When Orion passed behind the Moon, the Moon blocked direct communication with Earth.

questions.question: Why did engineers inspect Orion and analyze its data after Artemis II returned?
answers: To compare actual performance with predictions and improve spacecraft systems
To certify the heat shield without examining its actual flight performance
To assess only whether lunar surface experiments had been completed
To replace all qualification testing with a single launch result
questions.explanation: Post-flight analysis evaluates system performance and informs improvements.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly follows the main Artemis II mission phases?
answers: Lunar flyby, launch, atmospheric reentry, Earth-orbit checkouts
Earth-orbit checkouts, splashdown, launch, lunar flyby
Launch, Earth-orbit checkouts, lunar flyby, reentry and splashdown
Launch, lunar landing, Earth-orbit checkouts, splashdown
questions.explanation: The crew checked Orion near Earth, flew around the Moon, then returned through Earth's atmosphere.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the planned Artemis III demonstration?
answers: Reduce risk by testing spacecraft operations together
Carry astronauts around the Moon without docking
Repeat the uncrewed integrated SLS flight test
Demonstrate a complete crewed lunar descent
questions.explanation: Artemis III is designed to validate hardware and procedures before later crewed lunar landings.

questions.question: Where will Artemis III conduct its spacecraft demonstrations?
answers: The lunar surface
A transfer orbit to Mars
Orbit around the Moon
Low Earth orbit
questions.explanation: The current plan places Artemis III in low Earth orbit.

questions.question: According to NASA's October 2026 plan, when is Artemis III expected to launch?
questions.explanation: NASA's October 2026 mission plan targets a 2027 launch.

questions.question: How long is the Artemis III mission planned to last?
answers: About 14 days
About 2 days
About 30 days
About 10 days
questions.explanation: NASA describes a planned 14-day flight.

questions.question: How many astronauts are assigned to the planned Artemis III flight?
answers: Four
Three
Six
Two
questions.explanation: The announced crew consists of Randy Bresnik, Frank Rubio, Andre Douglas, and Luca Parmitano.

questions.question: Which spacecraft will the Artemis III crew launch and return in?
answers: Orion
Starship test article
The SLS core stage
Blue Moon Mark 2
questions.explanation: The crew will launch and return in Orion.

questions.question: Which rocket will launch the Artemis III crew aboard Orion?
answers: New Glenn
Vulcan
NASA's SLS
Falcon Heavy
questions.explanation: SLS is the launch vehicle for the crewed Orion spacecraft.

questions.question: How many commercial lander designs will Orion test with on Artemis III?
answers: Four
Two
Three
One
questions.explanation: The plan includes Blue Origin's Blue Moon and SpaceX's Starship test articles.

questions.question: Which two companies are developing the Artemis III lander test articles?
answers: Lockheed Martin and Northrop Grumman
Blue Origin and SpaceX
Boeing and Airbus
NASA and ESA
questions.explanation: Blue Origin and SpaceX provide the two commercial lander test articles.

questions.question: Which company is developing the Blue Moon Mark 2 test article?
answers: Boeing
SpaceX
Blue Origin
Airbus
questions.explanation: Blue Moon Mark 2 is Blue Origin's crewed lander architecture.

questions.question: Which version of Starship is planned as the basis for its Artemis III test article?
answers: Version 3
Version 5
Version 2
Version 1
questions.explanation: NASA's plan uses a Starship Version 3 test article.

questions.question: In the Artemis III plan, what does 'test article' mean?
answers: A rocket stage used only for launching satellites
A written mission summary prepared after landing
A spacecraft version built to evaluate selected capabilities
A vehicle approved for routine commercial passenger service
questions.explanation: The lander test articles demonstrate capabilities that inform later flight systems.

questions.question: Which launch order matches NASA's Artemis III plan?
answers: Orion, then Starship test article, then Blue Moon test article
